A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Informed Meta-Learning and the same Informed Neural Process framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable; v2 adds Appendix F.2–F.4.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, weather prediction, CUB image classification, and MNIST image-completion results in Section 4 and Appendix F.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on training-task scarcity, knowledge complexity, and spurious correlations in Appendix F.2–F.4.

M1.justification: The encoders, aggregation alternatives, latent predictive model, knowledge masking, and main ELBO objective in Equation 7 remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 revises the mathematical presentation of training without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: All original datasets and application domains remain. Appendix F.4 adds a distinct synthetic scenario with correlated training parameters and independent test parameters, extending the earlier frequency-distribution shift experiment. F.2–F.3 otherwise retain the existing regression task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same NP and informed/uninformed INP comparisons. The added experiments also compare INP with NP; the knowledge-complexity variants are controlled configurations of INP, not newly introduced competing methods.

E3.justification: F.2–F.4 substantially extend the evaluation design through training-task budgets from 25 to 1000, restricted training knowledge formats with common test knowledge, and six covariance settings evaluated on independent test parameters. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. F.3 has reporting inconsistencies, including a 500-task column absent from its stated training grid.

E4.justification: Three new analyses test generalization with fewer meta-training tasks, sensitivity to knowledge-space complexity, and robustness when training correlations disappear. Figures F.9–F.10 and Tables F.2–F.3 expose failure conditions beyond v1's knowledge-format and distribution-shift demonstrations.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 now identify their existing parenthesized quantities as standard errors over 110 weather tasks and 60 classification tasks per setting. Table F.3 adds significance-based bolding without specifying the test or threshold. Neither version documents seeds or repeated-training-run counts.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plotted results are retained, but F.2–F.4 add substantial new findings, including worse INP performance with insufficient training tasks and strong correlation shifts. For example, Table F.3 reports zero-context log likelihoods of -1367.3 for INP versus -410.7 for NP at correlation 0.99. These are newly evaluated conditions, not changes to earlier scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an explicit ELBO derivation using reweighting and Jensen's inequality. It consistently uses the variational conditional distribution and replaces v1's inconsistent minimization expression in Equation 11 with maximization of the derived ELBO. The principal formulation and Appendix E's uncertainty derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims: formalizing informed meta-learning, introducing INP as a proof of concept, and demonstrating potential data-efficiency and robustness benefits. The added failure studies qualify applicability without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the general expressiveness caveat into specific, empirically examined limitations involving insufficient training tasks, increasing knowledge complexity, and spurious correlations. F.2–F.4 explain failures through overfitting the relationship between knowledge and data. Section 3.4 also removes the general expectation that predictions without knowledge should perform no worse than NP.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a 0.3 knowledge-masking rate for sinusoidal regression, identifies 1000 training tasks for the original illustrative experiment, and discloses 60 evaluation tasks per classification setting. Hardware and optimizer details are relocated but unchanged, as are the code and generated-text availability statements.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Extended Related Work appendix are unchanged. Section 5 reuses existing NP references when discussing inherited limitations, without substantively changing the novelty claims or distinctions from prior approaches.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory expansions in Sections 2–4, revises the limitations discussion and training appendix, and adds acknowledgements and three appendix subsections. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact. Some editing defects remain or are introduced, including a duplicated sentence in Section 5 and an unresolved figure reference in Appendix D.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures F.9–F.10 and Tables F.2–F.3, expands the captions of Tables 2–3, and relocates several existing displays as text reflows. Existing graphical content and table structures are retained, with no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new scarcity and correlation-shift experiments turn generic limitations into demonstrated failure conditions, while Appendix A.2 resolves the inconsistent loss presentation and table captions clarify uncertainty reporting. These benefits are tempered by F.3's contradictory definition of M_b and a complexity trend that Table F.2 does not uniformly support, plus unspecified significance testing. The net improvement is useful but limited.
